To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce a new instance-aware 6D pose estimator that is robust to partial occlusions; (2) it is the first deep learning method for 6D object poses from RGB input that works robustly in the presence of occlusion; (3) it is also the first deep learning based 6D object estimator from RGB-D input that is able to handle partial occlusions; and (4) it is the only method that can handle occlusions for RGB and RGB

(1) we present the first deep-learning based system that estimates 6D poses of partly occluded rigid objects from RGB-D or RGB input, and (2) the system is based on a novel instance-aware 6D pose pipeline that is robust to occlusion, and hence can be used in many real-world scenarios.

we present the first system that estimates accurate 6D poses for partly occluders objects from RGB input, and that we achieve this with an instance-aware pipeline that eliminates surrounding clutter and object appearance, and that uses geometric optimization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the 6D poses of known rigid objects in the scene, given an image of that scene.
6D object instance localization, and 6D object localization and pose estimation in the presence of occlusions.
the problem of instance-aware 6D pose of known objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present the first deep-learning-based system for pose estimation of occluded objects from both RGB-D and RGB images.
the proposed iPose system is the state-of-the art system for 6D pose of known objects in partly occluded scenes from both RGB-D and RGB data.
the paper proposes a new pipeline for pose estimation of occluded objects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to show that accurate pose estimation is possible even for partly occluded 3D objects in single images.
we present a novel instance-aware approach to solve a difficult problem, and we achieve state-of-the-art results on a large benchmark for 6D pose.
we are the first method to estimate accurate 6D poses of partly occluded rigid objects using only RGB images.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of estimating 6D pose of partly occluded object is more easily solved by decomposing the problem into a sequence of easier problems.
the problem of 6D object detection is easier than previously thought, and we can achieve good pose estimation results by decomposing it into three simpler steps.
we demonstrate that deep learning can be used to solve complex problems by decomposing them into simpler sub-problems, and then solve each sub-problem using deep learning.
